title: Hobbycast Episode 13: Video Podcast - Asian Cinema Nostalgia - Part 6
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_wWswU9t8HU

The final flip-through, and Daniel (@dungeondive) saves several of his strongest opinions for it. *Infernal Affairs*, he argues, is flatly better than *The Departed*, and he suspects the remake only existed because American audiences still resisted Asian leading men. *Bio Zombie* is his favourite zombie comedy from any country, better than *Shaun of the Dead*, and the only film he knows where a Game Boy Camera is used to peek around corners. Patrick Tam's *The Sword*, one of the few wuxia films of the Hong Kong New Wave, sits in his all-time top ten and gets the loudest plea of the series to track it down.

There is a confession too: he owns no Bruce Lee films, only a pack of Bruceploitation knockoffs, and finds the real thing a little boring despite respecting the man. The oddities are the fun of this episode: *Legend of the Sacred Stone*, a wuxia epic performed entirely by marionettes and bought at Seattle's Scarecrow Video; *Yellow River Fighter*, a film he loves saddled with the worst dub he has heard; an early John Woo directing a young Jackie Chan in *Hand of Death*; and a Sonny Chiba box bought solely because it held *Ninja Wars*, the tape he rented endlessly from the store near his grandmother's house. *Kung Fu Zombie* closes the collection.

----

Daniel says Infernal Affairs beats The Departed on every count. Which remake do you think missed the point of its original?
